appraisal_events.evidence: un oncle de Swann... mourut, laissant toute cette fortune à Gilberte qui devenait ainsi une des plus riches héritières de France... Forcheville... déclara qu'il l'adoptait... Ce fut elle-même qui demanda à la duchesse de me « représenter » à elle.
appraisal_events.explanation: Gilberte inherits a vast fortune and is adopted and renamed by Forcheville, and in the passage's present scene she appears fully at ease inside Mme de Guermantes's own salon, directing her own introduction to the narrator -- the very circle that once refused to receive her as Mlle Swann.

appraisal_events.evidence: On sait que Mme de Guermantes... s'était, quand Swann s'était marié, refusée à recevoir sa fille aussi bien que sa femme.
appraisal_events.explanation: The passage reports, as a fact known to and remarked upon by her society, that the duchess refused for years to receive Swann's wife (and daughter), a socially registered exclusion tied to Odette's marriage to Swann.

status_effects.explanation: Her sudden fortune and her adoption/renaming by Forcheville visibly transform her standing, erasing the social liability of the name Swann.
As Mlle de Forcheville she is now fully inside Mme de Guermantes's salon, at ease enough to have herself presented to the narrator -- the same circle that had barred her as Mlle Swann.
As Swann's wife she was refused reception by the duchess for years, a publicly notable social exclusion.
